content.text: ▪︎fusion of left & right inferior renal poles
▪︎normal ascent interrupted as fused kidney gets caught
▪︎⇡ risk of renal stones, UPJ obstruction,
▪︎dilation of renal pelvis & calyces proximal to
: difficulty urinating; flank, back, &/or abdominal pain
(anechoic dilation of renal pelvis & calyces w/ distention of parenchyma)
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a relatively common genetic condition resulting from
Growth of numerous cysts in kidneys made of epithelial cells from renal tubules;
young pt w/ back/flank pain & HTN
: large renal size; multiple thin-walled cysts
HTN secondary to renal artery stenosis of 1 or both kidneys
: ⇣ renal blood flow leads to activation of RAAS
S/SXS: HA, <20yo or >50yo w/ HTN, severe HTN, HTN resistant to 3 or more drugs
